hypothesis.title: Measure whether the four crash_after_send_* anchors ever fire before adding or retiring anchor machinery
hypothesis.description: One-iteration, semantics-free measurement in spur/spur-core/src/simulator/: for each of the four crash_after_send_* params, increment a util_stats counter when the anchor condition is offered and when a crash is actually injected at that anchor (crash_anchor.<param>.offered / .applied). Emit in the existing stats block that already carries aos.tape_wins and dedup.checks under stats:true. No new config fields, no default changes, no eval-harness or gate changes, no touch of core/exec.rs.
hypothesis.rationale: Three pool items hinge on one unmeasured integer: retire-send-anchored-crash-params (blocked, best gain/cost in pool, dead-code removal), and any further crash-anchor add. The utilization audit lists aos/dedup/stale_accept as zero-activity but says nothing about the send-anchored crash path; if applied==0 the entire anchored-crash family (send-anchored-crash-points, delayed-send-anchored-crash, crash-boost-dose-sweep — all closed at ~0.0002 or less) was unmeasurable by construction, which retroactively explains those nulls and makes deletion free. Unlike acted-fraction-instrumentation, the number lands in a stats block that is already read at audit time, adds zero general config params, and is not on the dispatch hot path.
hypothesis.generalityArgument: Counters over existing crash-injection code paths keyed by config param name; no protocol vocabulary, no behavioral change on any spec.
hypothesis.notes: Red team: this is telemetry, and the observations log is explicit that telemetry merges that feed no gate produced zero decision value. Accepted only because it is pre-committed to a decision: applied==0 => unblock and execute retire-send-anchored-crash-params and reject all new anchor proposals; applied>0 => the anchored-crash nulls stand as real and the family is closed for good.
